notes: Juniper Fenn (bible 5.6), fletcher and herbalist, laconic, sunburnt, knows the Briarwood. Fears fire; the silence of the wolves frightens her more than howling. Secret: her sleep-draughts make the song easier to follow, and she has just worked it out (option ask-draughts). Class reactions per bible: archer peer, knight 'you'll clank', sorcerer trades herbs for Nature scraps, thief gets poisons only after a favour (the thief option checks disposition >= 10, which the draught talk can raise). Merchant greeting and farewell lines vary by class; the counter itself is the shop. mw-e39.10 (The Captain's Boots): ask-hale (she has seen the dust on her step, boots.noticed), bring-bellwort (two bellwort roots from her own counter become wakeful tea, juniper.tea-ready, handed to Hale in hale-watch) and ask-sleep-draught (the wrong draught: she warns if she has already confessed, then sells it, juniper.draught-sold).

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: You'll clank. Everything in the Briarwood will hear you. That's fine. It'll hear you coming and leave. What do you need?

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Archer. Good. Somebody who knows a string from a snare. Don't touch the yew until I've waxed it. What can I do for you?

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Sorcerer. I've no use for flash. I do have a use for anything Nature-school you've got scraps of. Herbs for scraps. Fair? What do you need?

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Hm. Hands where I can see them. I don't judge what you take. I judge what you do with it. What do you need?

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Fenn's. Arrows, snares, salves. Don't ask for a refund. What do you need?

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Back. Good. Say what you need. Or say nothing. Either's fine.

options.text: Your sleep-draughts. Half the town buys them.
Anything about trail lore or trick arrows?
What would you give me for Nature-school scraps?
Is my armour really that loud?
I hear you keep things for the careful.
Captain Hale's boots are dusty every morning.
I have the two bellwort roots for the wakeful tea.
Have you a sleep draught? For the captain.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Wolves don't go quiet. Not unless something bigger is listening. Three weeks ago they stopped. I don't know a Briarwood without howling. It's like being in a house with the clocks stopped.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: A line of trampled ferns, running toward the mine. You can only see it at night or if you know how to look. I found it. I haven't followed it. I'm told I'm very sensible. I'd rather be brave.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Aye. Sleep-draughts. I've sold them to half the town for the wolves' howling. I thought I was selling rest. This week I worked it out. They sleep deeper. And deeper they hear it clearer.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: The song. I've been selling people an easier way to follow it. I haven't slept since. Tell me I'm wrong. Please. You'd be the first.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Maybe. Maybe not. I'll brew wakeful tea instead, and stop selling the other. It won't bring anyone back. But it's a thing I can do with my hands.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Aye. They are. I know. I counted. I'm not asking you to be kind. I'm asking you to be right. You are. I'll make the wakeful tea.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Peer to peer: fire-arrows spook wolves and nothing else, and a snare line sings if you wet it. Tell me what you'd like and I'll set the price at what I'd charge myself.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Scraps of Nature-school for good herbs. Bring me anything that grows when it shouldn't. I'll bring you what grows when it should. That's a fair trade in any country.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Like a cart of kettles. It's no insult. A loud knight is a kindness to everything else in the Briarwood, who get to leave. Oil the joints. That's free advice.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: You did right by me. Ask at the counter. Quietly. What I keep under it is for the careful, and the careful pay in advance.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: I don't sell poisons to strangers. Do me a favour first. Hear me out on a thing that's keeping me up, and ask me again.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Mind the clank. Mind the trees. Mind your feet.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Good shooting. Wax the string.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Mind the herbs. If it grows back, it's yours.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Come back when you need a thing, quietly.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Walk careful. Light a lamp.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: I know. Prints on my step before dawn: big boots, mine dust to the ankle. Walks past my door with his eyes shut, like a man late for church. I thought I was seeing things. I haven't been sleeping.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: He won't take a draught, if he's any sense. What he wants is a wakeful tea. Keeps you up, not out. Two roots of bellwort from the counter here, bring them back, and I'll brew it. If he'll drink it.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: And if you've a mind to sell him sleep instead, I'm not telling you what to do. I'm telling you what I'd do.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Good roots. Not the sulky ones from the south bank. Give me a minute and a kettle, and don't watch it, it goes shy.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: There. Don't let it go cold; it turns the colour of a bad tooth. It wants carrying to the Watch House. I'd carry it myself, but he looks at me as if I might ask him about wolves.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: I told you what they do. They sleep deeper, and deeper they hear it clearer. And you want one for a man who already walks. ...I'll sell it. It's your conscience. I won't carry mine again.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Sleep draught. Eight crowns. Blue bottle, two spoons, never three. It'll give the captain a night's rest such as he hasn't had in years.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Two spoons. Never three. And if he sleeps too well, that is a thing I will have to live with.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Eight crowns, the purse says seven and a sigh. Come back when it's heavier.

nodes.speaker: juniper
nodes.text: Good. I'm glad. Don't tell me I'm sensible.
